root_cause: The replacement path negotiated and activated native media without registering the signed lifecycle writer used by ordinary connections. Epoch-tagged video reached the new client, but its authenticated epoch notice was never emitted. The client correctly expired the packet at its unchanged 200ms deadline.
fix: Capture the original signed lifecycle registration during native replacement negotiation, without retaining its invocation or Store reader. Attach it to the same physical peer only after ordinary activation is published. Every notification uses current entry, credential, physical lifetime and media authority checks. Failed attachment settles the known movement as stopped; no second movement or media replay.
scope: Two real enrolled EdDSA SDK peers establish audio/video and original video history.
The original replacement operation allocates, negotiates and commits generation-two native resources, transferring both existing video directions.
Replacement receiver admits authenticated current epochs, emits actual feedback, and receives a freshly encoded keyframe independently decoded at original RTP6000.
Retained receiver requests recovery from the raw replacement publisher; the hint is consumed once before fresh encoding, and the fresh key independently decodes at original RTP12000.
Original operation, source frames, SSRCs and RTP clocks are retained. Owned peers, encoder and server join.
